## Objective
Connect v8-next economic evaluation to two physically produced native/reference ledgers with explicit semantic mapping and fail-closed parity receipts.

## Owning authority
- D-116 independent economic parity.
- D-153 §2.3 and §2.6.
- docs/contracts/PARITY_AND_IDENTITY_SPEC.md
- Related existing issue #329.

## Change class
CONTRACT_IMPLEMENTATION

## Current state
v8-next parity.py already defines ArtifactBinding, SemanticMapping, ParityReceipt, and physical ledger loading. The economic command records engine rerun parity and artifact hashes, but does not require or consume an external reference ledger for the benchmark result; monetary reconciliation gaps remain.

## Required end state
R1 — Require native and reference ledgers declared by a benchmark manifest.
R2 — Pair records by the versioned mapping and compare exact bit-pattern values where the contract requires it.
R3 — Record missing/unpaired/unsupported semantics as explicit outcomes, never zero differences.
R4 — Bind parity receipt identity to policy, case, mapping, engine, artifact hashes, and method version.
R5 — Keep parity diagnostic and non-sovereign.

## Expected file / module surface
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/parity.py
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/economic_benchmark.py
v8-next/src/v8_next/app/economic.py
v8-next/src/v8_next/evaluation/benchmark_receipt.py
v8-next/tests/test_d153_parity.py
v8-next/tests/test_economic_parity_wiring.py (new)

## Verification gates
Test missing/tampered/empty artifacts, schema/mapping mismatch, unpaired records, bit-pattern divergence, policy identity binding, receipt grafting, and economic CLI integration with two physical ledgers.

## Required evidence artifacts
Native/reference physical ledger files; manifest; semantic mapping hash; engine/method versions; ParityReceipt; reconciliation gap report; reproducible integration output.

## Non-goals / forbidden scope
No fixed vectors, no tolerance-based economic pass, no fabricated zero metrics, no external authority promotion, and no synthetic production ledger.

### Context-completeness contract

### 11. Normative Traceability
R1 — Two physical artifacts are mandatory for external parity. Authority: D-116/D-153.
R2 — Missing is not zero. Authority: parity.py.
R3 — External parity cannot mint economic authority.

### 12. Existing Types / Interfaces to Reuse
Reuse ArtifactBinding, ParitySubject, SemanticMapping, EngineVersion, ParityReceipt, benchmark receipt binding, and existing DATA_BLOCKED/PARITY outcomes.

### 13. Mathematical / Semantic Invariants
I1: parity digest changes when policy/mapping/engine/artifact identity changes.
I2: exact float equality uses IEEE-754 bit patterns where required.
I3: monetary fields absent from both ledgers remain explicit gaps.

### 14. Canonical Failure Semantics
Missing artifact -> DATA_BLOCKED.
Pairing mismatch -> UNPAIRED_RECORDS.
Unsupported semantics -> UNSUPPORTED_SEMANTICS.
Divergence -> PARITY_DIVERGED.
Parity never upgrades claim authority.

### 15. Dependency Map
benchmark manifest -> native/reference bindings -> semantic mapping -> parity receipt -> economic receipt/report.

### 16. Ambiguity / OPEN_PIN Triggers
- If an owning contract or estimand is ambiguous, STOP and open an OPEN_PIN.
- If an artifact cannot be physically produced and hashed, STOP; do not substitute it.
- If the requested behavior would open protected OOS or mint authority, STOP pending explicit governance.

### References / sources / attachments
Related: #329 and #323. v8-next parity adapter exists but default economic command does not wire the external reference ledger.

### V8 guards
- [x] I will not invent a new canonical error code, ontology, or parallel interface unless an R# requirement explicitly authorizes it.
- [x] No unrelated semantic strategy change is bundled into this implementation issue.
- [x] No frozen OOS is opened unless this issue explicitly carries that authority.
- [x] If the owning contract is ambiguous, I will open/escalate an OPEN_PIN rather than invent an interpretation.
